proved: The product exposes a separate Share full review with project action only after a completed response; a pending native source-locator continuation cannot be archived.

The archive binds the exact frozen request and sources, normalized response and retained tool proposals, Rust-authored content-free run record, project/document/editor source revision, save-time Yjs revision, author snapshot, and timestamp under one canonical SHA-256.
Cross-field validation requires matching run, call, provider, model, task, source IDs, limits, terminal success, and public provider-run semantics before any write.

Stale research, including a collaborator change during archive hashing, malformed or oversized history, hostile terminal state or timestamps, duplicate local run identity, and provenance substitution fail before mutation.
Peer-namespaced same-run archives converge; divergent canonical hashes remain an explicit blocking conflict with no selected archive.

Routine product and MCP research inspection returns metadata, counts, byte totals, and conflicts without question, source, response, or tool-proposal bodies; the product loads a full verified archive only after explicit selection.
The archive commits before best-effort attribution under the closed provider-review research-event kind; signing failure remains explicit unsigned and does not roll back the archive.
Neither the archive model nor the history view imports an editor mutation operation, and product copy states that sharing never changes the policy draft.
Platform contracts expose the exact implementation status and watchdog-wrapped self-check separately from live-provider or packaged evidence.
notProved: Packaged native Send once plus Share interaction, restart/reopen rendering, or accessibility/visual behavior on any operating system.
Physical two-install propagation through Drive or the bundled relay, concurrent live clicking, transport interruption, quota, or recovery behavior.
Near-8-MiB archive rendering, 32-MiB history memory use, retention/compaction/repair usability, or performance on low-memory machines.
Live provider compatibility, accuracy, retention, cost, billing, rate limits, or policy compliance.
Authenticated human or organizational authorship; the signature proves only possession of a self-issued registered installation key.
History for failed, cancelled, timed-out, or disclosure-denied ordinary provider calls.
